title: An apology you can rely on

captions.emotions: Feeling stability in an honest promise

meaning: Familiar words of apology can offer support when honest terms and a continuation understandable to both people stand behind them.
text: “I’m sorry” can be a recognised expression of respect and the beginning of a precise exchange. The Hierophant in the physical position of Vishuddha appears through an accepted way of acknowledging an error and speaking about mutual obligations. Justice in energy supports honesty: words need to relate to each person’s actual participation. The Emperor in emotions gives stability when a promise becomes understandable. An apology can become easier to rely on when it expresses a particular meaning beyond restoring an outwardly correct conversational order.

For example, an argument produced a promise of help that could not be fulfilled. A familiar apology receives a continuation: which words were hasty and which reply is realistic now. **Support grows from an honest continuation of familiar words.** You can acknowledge an error without promising to repair everything immediately. Understandable participation gives greater certainty than a solemn phrase surrounded by the old guesses. Both people know which commitment actually exists.

The difficulty begins if restoring order makes an apology the final closure of the subject. The other person still needs to explain what hurt while conversation already demands movement onwards. Honest responsibility remains meaningful. Stability becomes more alive when a recognised formula leaves room for that reply alongside a new schedule of practical actions.
